newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen consolidating, focus on auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen consolidating, focus on auction.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to consolidate at the higher end of 124-125 on Tuesday after it failed to stay above 125.00 on Monday.

The focus will be on the Finance Ministry's auction of 20-year JGBs, which are expected to be offered in a volume of 400 billion yen and with a coupon rate of 3.1 percent, as well as on the launch of 100 billion yen worth of 10-year straight bonds by Tokyo Electric Power Co Ltd, traders said.
"The market may start another rally if these long-term bonds are absorbed well," said a securities house dealer.
The September fell close to its session low on Monday after rising for four consecutive days last week.

"It is an adjustment period after the September rose too quickly last week. The contract is likely to follow the current downtrend rather than rise further," said a dealer at a trust bank's securities unit.
The target for the contract is 124.73 against Monday's close of 124.83. The 65-day moving average of 124.65 is likely to provide another support, traders said.
MOF is expected to announce an offer of 20-year JGBs at 10.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
